chapters.title: Newton's second law — net force and acceleration
chapters.content: For a body of constant mass, net external force is the product of mass and acceleration: F = ma. Force is measured in newtons (N), mass in kilograms (kg), and acceleration in metres per second squared (m/s²). This is a model of classical mechanics, not a statement that every possible force problem follows F = ma without conditions.

chapters.title: Kinetic energy of a moving body
chapters.content: In non-relativistic classical mechanics, kinetic energy equals one half of mass multiplied by speed squared: K = 1/2 mv². This expression is an approximation when the speed is much smaller than the speed of light.

chapters.title: Conservation of linear momentum
chapters.content: In an isolated system with no net external force, the total linear momentum remains constant. The momentum of a particle in the classical model is its mass times its velocity: p = mv.
